title: rootful inter-container dns not working with custom dns_bind_port on internal bridge networks
body:
### Issue Description

Hello, I have seen some other issues somewhat related but nothing quite like this so forgive me if this is a duplicate. Basically as the title suggests. inter-container dns resolution in internal bridge networks seems to not work when the `dns_bind_port` value has been set to something other than 53. This is not the case for non-internal networks which is why I think this might be a bug. Thanks for your time! 

### Steps to reproduce the issue

```toml
File: /etc/containers/containers.conf
[network]
dns_bind_port = 54
```
 
1. `podman network create --internal t1`
2. `podman run --rm -d --cap-add CAP_NET_RAW --network t1 --name c1 alpine sleep 1h`
3. `podman run --rm -d --cap-add CAP_NET_RAW --network t1 --name c2 alpine sleep 1h`
4. `podman exec c1 ping c2`
>	ping: bad address 'c2'
5. `podman kill c1 c2`
6. `podman network create t2`
7. `podman run --rm -d --cap-add CAP_NET_RAW --network t2 --name c1 alpine sleep 1h`
8. `podman run --rm -d --cap-add CAP_NET_RAW --network t2 --name c2 alpine sleep 1h`
9. `podman exec c3 ping c4`
> 	PING c4 (10.89.3.6): 56 data bytes
> 	64 bytes from 10.89.3.6: seq=0 ttl=64 time=0.019 ms
> 	64 bytes from 10.89.3.6: seq=1 ttl=64 time=0.048 ms
> 	64 bytes from 10.89.3.6: seq=2 ttl=64 time=0.044 ms

- `ss -tunlp | rg ':5(3|4)\b'`
```
udp   UNCONN 0      0                           10.89.2.1:54         0.0.0.0:*    users:(("aardvark-dns",pid=1392477,fd=11))
tcp   LISTEN 0      128                         10.89.2.1:54         0.0.0.0:*    users:(("aardvark-dns",pid=1392477,fd=12))
```

### Describe the results you received

Container c2 was resolved normally but not on an internal network from c1. 

### Describe the results you expected

for both internal and non-internal networks to behave the same since that is the behavior when `dns_bind_port` is set to 53

### podman info output

```yaml
podman version 6.1.4 on archlinux (linux/amd64)
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Privileged

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes
